name: Koshary
description: Egypt's beloved national dish — a hearty mix of rice, lentils, pasta, and chickpeas topped with a spiced tomato sauce and crispy fried onions.
steps: Cook lentils in salted water until tender, then drain.
Cook rice separately and mix with lentils while warm.
Boil macaroni until al dente, drain and set aside.
Fry sliced onions in oil until deeply golden and crispy. Remove and drain.
In the same pan, sauté garlic, add crushed tomatoes, vinegar, cumin, salt, and pepper. Simmer 15 minutes.
To serve: layer rice-lentil mix, then macaroni, then chickpeas.
Top with tomato sauce and crispy onions.

name: Molokhya
description: A rich, velvety green soup made from jute leaves, simmered with chicken broth and finished with a fragrant garlic and coriander ta'leya.
steps: Bring chicken broth to a boil in a large pot.
Add frozen molokhya and stir until fully thawed and simmering.
Season with salt and simmer on low for 5 minutes.
Crush garlic with a pinch of salt until it forms a paste.
Melt butter in a small pan, add garlic paste and ground coriander. Fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour the garlic ta'leya into the soup and stir immediately.
Serve hot over white rice with a side of chicken and bread.

name: Macarona Bashamel
description: Egypt's iconic baked pasta — layers of macaroni and spiced minced meat smothered in a thick, creamy béchamel sauce and baked until golden.
steps: Cook pasta until al dente, drain and set aside.
Sauté diced onion until soft, add minced beef and cook until browned. Stir in tomato paste, salt, and pepper.
Make béchamel: melt butter, whisk in flour for 1 minute, then gradually add milk whisking constantly until thick.
Remove béchamel from heat, season with nutmeg and salt, then beat in eggs quickly.
In a greased baking dish layer: half the pasta, all the meat, remaining pasta.
Pour béchamel over the top, spreading evenly.
Bake at 180°C for 35–40 minutes until the top is deep golden.

name: Chicken Ranch
description: Tender grilled chicken marinated in ranch spices, served with a tangy homemade ranch dipping sauce and fresh vegetables.
steps: Mix olive oil, garlic powder, onion powder, dill, parsley, paprika, salt, pepper, and lemon juice.
Score the chicken breasts and coat thoroughly with the marinade.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight.
Grill over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes per side until cooked through.
Let rest 5 minutes before slicing.
Serve with ranch dipping sauce and a fresh salad.

name: Macarona bil Lahma
description: A comforting Egyptian stovetop pasta — macaroni simmered in a rich, spiced tomato and beef sauce until it soaks up all the flavour.
steps: Sauté diced onion and garlic in oil until golden.
Add minced beef and cook until browned, breaking up any lumps.
Stir in tomato sauce, 7-spice, salt, and pepper. Simmer 10 minutes.
Add raw macaroni to the sauce with enough water to cover by 2cm.
Cook on medium heat, stirring occasionally, until pasta is tender and sauce is absorbed.
Adjust seasoning and serve hot.

name: Hummus
description: Creamy and smooth chickpea dip infused with tahini, lemon, and garlic — a classic Egyptian appetizer served with warm pita bread.
steps: Drain chickpeas and reserve 1/2 cup of the canning liquid.
Add chickpeas, tahini, lemon juice, and garlic to a food processor.
Blend until smooth, adding chickpea liquid gradually until you reach desired consistency.
Season with salt and cumin.
Transfer to a serving bowl and drizzle with olive oil.
Garnish with paprika and serve with pita bread.

name: Baba Ganoush
description: Smoky and silky eggplant dip made with tahini and lemon, perfect as a starter or mezze platter addition.
steps: Prick eggplants and roast over open flame or in oven at 200°C until charred and soft (20-30 minutes).
Let cool, then scoop out the flesh and discard the skin.
Add eggplant flesh, tahini, lemon juice, and garlic to a food processor.
Blend until creamy and smooth.
Season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle with olive oil and garnish with pomegranate seeds.
Serve with pita bread or vegetables.

name: Muhammarah
description: A vibrant red pepper and walnut dip with a tangy pomegranate twist, a delicious appetizer from the Levantine tradition.
steps: Roast red peppers over an open flame until charred on all sides.
Place in a plastic bag for 10 minutes to steam, then peel off the skin.
Remove stems and seeds, then chop the peppers.
In a food processor, blend peppers, walnuts, pomegranate molasses, breadcrumbs, and garlic.
Add olive oil and blend until smooth and creamy.
Season with salt and cumin.
Serve with pita bread and drizzle with more olive oil.

name: Kunafa
description: A crispy and sweet Egyptian pastry layered with cheese and shredded pastry, baked until golden and drizzled with fragrant simple syrup.
steps: Make simple syrup: boil sugar and water for 10 minutes, add lemon juice and rose water, then cool completely.
Soak kunafa pastry in melted butter until well coated.
Layer half the buttered kunafa in a greased baking dish.
Slice akkawi cheese thinly and layer over the pastry.
Top with remaining kunafa and press gently.
Bake at 180°C for 25-30 minutes until golden brown.
Pour cooled syrup over the hot kunafa immediately after baking.
Garnish with crushed pistachios and serve warm.

name: Basboosa
description: Sweet coconut and semolina cake topped with an almond, soaked in aromatic simple syrup — a beloved Egyptian treat.
steps: Mix semolina, coconut, yogurt, sugar, and baking powder until well combined.
Press the mixture into a greased 9x13 inch pan, smoothing the top.
Cut into diamond or square shapes and place an almond in the center of each piece.
Bake at 160°C for 25-30 minutes until light golden.
Meanwhile, boil sugar and water for 10 minutes, add rose water, then cool completely.
Pour cold syrup over hot basboosa immediately after removing from oven.
Let cool before serving. Store in an airtight container.

name: Umm Ali
description: A luxurious Egyptian bread pudding made with puff pastry, milk, and nuts — traditionally served warm as the ultimate comfort dessert.
steps: Layer puff pastry sheets on a baking tray and bake at 200°C for 10-12 minutes until golden and crispy.
Cool pastry, then tear into large bite-sized pieces and layer in a baking dish.
Scatter nuts and raisins over the pastry pieces.
Heat milk and coconut milk together, then stir in sugar until dissolved.
Add vanilla extract, then pour the hot milk mixture over the pastry.
Bake at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until the top is light brown.
Serve warm, garnished with cinnamon and additional nuts.
